problems: [hook] "80 की उम्र में दादी की लिस्ट में क्या था?" — this is a contents-page hook, banned by STORY.md §1; the hook should open a curiosity gap with an image or number, not announce a list.

[shape] Beats 1–4 are four parallel joyful activities (pizza, dance, flight, selfie) with no escalation, no obstacle, no turn — they could be swapped with no loss, making the reel a listicle, not a story (STORY.md §2).
[concrete] No specific, physical detail survives — no name, date, count, or unique object; the pizza, dance, flight, and actor are generic (STORY.md §3).

[dialogue] All four list lines are literary, not spoken Hindi — "बिल्कुल मेरे बचपन की मिठाई जैसा", "जीवन का जश्न मनाते हुए", "दिल की धड़कन जैसे तड़प रही है", "जिंदादिली" — a grandmother would not say these (STORY.md §4).
[budget] Beat 1 line is 20 words for a 7 s clip (≈2.9 wps), beats 2–4 are 15 words each (≈2.1 wps) — spoken Hindi runs ~2.2 wps, so lines must be ~13 words for 6 s of speech (STORY.md §4).

[moral] The moral card contains two sentences, the second a direct question to the viewer ("पूछिए...") — a question is a CTA, not a moral; also the platitude "सपनों की कोई उम्र नहीं होती" is unsupported because the story never shows her dream being doubted (STORY.md §5).

[sameness] This reel replicates the already-shipped `dadi-ki-bucket-list` (same hook card, same four list beats, same grandson Q&A, same moral, same CTA) — STORY.md §6 forbids repeating a prior reel's architecture.
[length] The brief requires each clip ~10 s with 6–9 s of speech, but the script allocates only 7 s per clip, leaving no room for the required speech duration (Idea brief).
[hook] "80 की उम्र में दादी की लिस्ट में क्या था?" — contents-page hook announces a list; STORY.md §1 bans preface/contents-page openings (mandated by brief but still a structural flaw).
[shape] Beats 1–4 are parallel bucket-list items with no causal escalation and no turn; swapping any two loses nothing — a listicle, not a story. STORY.md §2.
[concrete] No specific surviving detail — "पिज़्ज़ा", "नाचना", "हवाई जहाज", "सेल्फी" are generic categories; nothing a viewer could name after watching. STORY.md §3.

[dialogue] All four list lines are written Hindi, not spoken — "आख़िर आ गया मेरा पिज़्ज़ा — भूख मिट गई, दिल भर गया!", "ऐसा स्वाद आया कि पाँव खुद थिरकने लगे!", "पिज़्ज़ा ने याद दिलाया — मुझे भी तो उड़ना था!", "देखो, मेरे हीरो मेरे साथ सेल्फी ले रहे हैं!" — no grandmother speaks this way. STORY.md §4.
[budget] Every list line is 10–13 words for 7s of speech (1.4–1.9 wps) — spoken Hindi needs ~2.2 wps; lines will leave 3–4s dead air per clip. STORY.md §4.
[moral] "सपनों की कोई उम्र नहीं होती। पूछिए, आपके घर के बुज़ुर्गों की इच्छा क्या है?" — first sentence is a platitude unsupported by the montage; second is a CTA question, not a moral. STORY.md §5.
[sameness] Structure (hook-card → four parallel list beats → grandson Q&A → moral-card → CTA-card) and moral duplicate shipped reels "dadi-ki-bucket-list" and "dadi-bucket-list". STORY.md §6.
